canonical_statement: The study aimed to characterize long-term disease-specific and general health-related quality of life and depressive symptoms in hemifacial spasm patients receiving repeated Abo-botulinum toxin A treatment over five years.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This study aimed to determine the long-term quality of life (QoL) in hemifacial spasm (HFS) patients after treating with Abo-botulinum toxin A (Abo-BTX).

canonical_statement: The study was a five-year prospective repeated-measures study in which Abo-botulinum toxin A was administered at three-month intervals.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The five-year prospective study of the quality of life for HFS patients treated with Abo-BTX A injections at three-month intervals was designed

canonical_statement: Eligible participants had hemifacial spasm, were 18 to 80 years old, and could provide reliable answers to Thai-language HRQoL questionnaires.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: All HFS patients, aged between 18 and 80 years, who provided reliable answers to the HRQoL questionnaires (Thai version) were included in this study.

inclusion_criteria: Reliable answers to Thai-language HRQoL questionnaires

canonical_statement: Exclusion criteria included lack of informed consent, potential pregnancy without proper contraception or lactation, significant medical conditions that could influence trial evaluations, and history of allergy to botulinum toxin A.

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that Abo-botulinum toxin A improved quality of life during the first few years of treatment, but only the SF-36 general health domain remained significantly improved across five years.

canonical_statement: The authors proposed that the relationship between neutralizing antibodies against Abo-botulinum toxin A and declining long-term quality of life should be evaluated in future studies.
